prompt.context: The client is a $250 million Performance Chemicals division of a $7 billion Specialty Chemicals Company. The CEO of the parent company has set a 'growth agenda' — he believes his company can become the fastest growing chemical company, moving from 3–4% historical growth to 10–15% growth, and has asked all business units to develop and present growth strategies. Performance Chemicals' business manager, like many other managers, does not believe there is significant untapped potential in the markets his unit currently serves. He has approached Deloitte Consulting for strategic advice.
prompt.question: How would you go about building a case for whether or not the Performance Chemicals division can grow at a 10%+ per annum rate? How will you approach this problem? Develop potential growth strategies and recommendations for the Performance Chemicals management team.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current growth rate of the division and its markets?
clarifying_info.a: All 6 businesses within the division have been growing at 3–4% for the last 5 years, which matches the average growth rate of the markets they serve.

clarifying_info.q: What types of products does the Performance Chemicals division sell?
clarifying_info.a: Products include asphalt additives, sodium chemicals, and paper pulp bleaching solutions, among others.

clarifying_info.q: How would you describe the competitive environment?
clarifying_info.a: All products have limited intellectual property protection and are threatened by global competition. Commoditization and pricing pressures are constraining growth.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any cultural or organizational factors to be aware of?
clarifying_info.a: Yes. Like most chemical companies, the client has focused solely on selling products and has not actively sought growth ideas. A representative quote from the client: 'We make it by the ton and sell it by the carload.'

framework: 1. Understand the current market position: assess market size, growth rates, customers, and competitive dynamics for each of the 6 business lines
2. Identify cultural and organizational impediments: evaluate whether the product-centric culture can support a new growth agenda
3. Build a Growth Spectrum: explore opportunities across Product Enhancements, New Products, New Markets, New Channels, and New Business Models
4. Assess feasibility of each strategy: consider company capabilities, required investments, and fit with existing assets
5. Develop prioritized recommendations: select strategies with highest impact and feasibility, and outline implementation path

questions.prompt: What does the existing business analysis reveal about the likelihood of hitting 10%+ growth through organic means?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note that 3–4% growth across all 6 businesses mirrors the market growth rate, suggesting no outperformance. Limited IP protection and commoditization mean organic product-led growth is unlikely to close the gap. The candidate should conclude that the company must look beyond traditional product strategy.

questions.prompt: What industry or macro trends might unlock new growth avenues for a specialty chemicals company?
questions.guidance: Strong answers mention: outsourcing (customers outsourcing chemical management to the supplier), solutions vs. products (moving from selling a chemical to selling an outcome), product-service bundles (combining chemicals with application expertise or monitoring services), and digitization or supply chain integration.

questions.prompt: What alternative growth strategies should Performance Chemicals consider?
questions.guidance: Candidate should generate a structured list of strategies. Strong answers include: (1) Sell a solution not a product — bundle expertise and outcomes with chemicals; (2) Become indispensable to strategic customers — deepen relationships with key accounts to become a preferred or sole-source supplier; (3) Become a one-stop shop for specialty chemicals — expand the product portfolio so customers consolidate purchasing; (4) Vendor managed inventory (VMI) as a service — take over customers' chemical inventory management to create stickiness and recurring revenue. Candidate may also suggest new market entry using existing technological capabilities.

questions.prompt: What is the potential scale of the opportunity if growth strategies are successfully executed?
questions.guidance: Preliminary projections from the Deloitte engagement indicated potential to quadruple the size of the Performance Chemicals group from $250 million to $1 billion in 5 years. Candidate should be able to back-of-envelope verify: $250M growing at ~32% CAGR over 5 years ≈ $1B (or alternatively, $250M × 4 = $1B in absolute terms). This far exceeds the CEO's 10–15% target.

math.setup: If Performance Chemicals grows from $250M to $1B in 5 years, what is the implied CAGR?
math.answer: Approximately 32% CAGR, implying quadrupling the division in 5 years — well above the CEO's 10–15% target.

brainstorming.prompt: What growth strategies could the Performance Chemicals division pursue beyond traditional product sales?

categories.name: Product and Portfolio Expansion
ideas: Develop higher-margin specialty variants with stronger IP protection
Expand into adjacent chemical categories to become a one-stop shop
Invest in R&D to create proprietary formulations less exposed to commoditization

categories.name: New Business Models
ideas: Shift from product sales to outcome-based contracts (e.g., sell 'road durability' not asphalt additive)
Offer vendor managed inventory (VMI) as a paid service
Bundle chemicals with monitoring, testing, or application services

categories.name: Customer Strategy
ideas: Focus on becoming indispensable to 10–20 strategic accounts
Create switching costs through deep process integration
Develop co-innovation programs with key customers

categories.name: New Markets and Channels
ideas: Apply existing chemical technology capabilities in new end markets (e.g., water treatment, agriculture)
Enter emerging markets where commoditization has not yet occurred
Use digital channels or e-commerce to reach mid-market customers at lower cost

categories.name: Outsourcing and Services
ideas: Offer chemical procurement outsourcing for customers who want to simplify supply chains
Manage on-site chemical operations for large industrial customers
Provide technical advisory services tied to product usage

recommendation: Performance Chemicals should pursue a multi-pronged growth strategy anchored in transitioning from a product seller to a solutions and services provider

Priority strategies are: (1) product-service bundling for top accounts, (2) vendor managed inventory as a recurring revenue service, and (3) leveraging existing technology capabilities to enter adjacent markets
These strategies, combined, have the potential to quadruple division revenues to $1 billion within 5 years, well exceeding the CEO's 10–15% growth target
risks: Cultural resistance: the 'make it by the ton, sell it by the carload' mindset may hinder adoption of service-oriented models
Capability gaps: delivering solutions and services requires talent and systems the division may lack today
Execution complexity: pursuing multiple strategies simultaneously may dilute focus and resources
Margin risk: if the transition to services is not priced correctly, margins may not improve despite revenue growth
next_steps: Conduct a growth diagnostic to identify cultural and infrastructural impediments
Run 2-day strategy workshops with each of the 6 niche business units to develop tailored growth strategies
Develop preliminary financial projections for the top 2–3 strategies per business unit
Build an implementation roadmap and secure CEO alignment on prioritized initiatives
